<!-- plain-summary -->
A deployment supervisor (systemd, k8s, a load balancer) has no way to ask a wyrd process "are you alive, and are you ready to serve?" — today the only signal is whether the process exists. This wires the standard gRPC health protocol (`tonic-health`) into the server roles, reflecting the storage backend's own `health()` state, so an unhealthy store flips the readiness probe instead of silently serving errors.

**Parent:** #366 (floor item 5). Spec: proposal 0010 (`docs/design/proposals/draft/0010-observability-floor-for-first-deployment.md`), §"Scope boundary" item 7 (`tonic-health` liveness/readiness reflecting `health()`).

## Scope (from 0010)

- `tonic-health` service on the gRPC role entries; readiness derived from the `Health` enum / `health()` at the `crates/traits` seam.
- The DST property 0010 names: an unhealthy store flips the readiness probe.

## Notes

- 0010's companion DST properties attach per slice; the probe property belongs to this one.
